claims.explanation: Monastrol is a specific inhibitor of the mitotic kinesin KIF11 (Eg5), which is required for centrosome separation and bipolar spindle assembly; sensitivity should therefore track with dependence on KIF11-driven spindle function and with an intact, checkpoint-competent mitotic machinery. Lines that are most killed are enriched for TP53 pathway loss plus proliferative/RTK-RAS and chromatin-remodeler mutations, whereas many resistant lines carry alterations that blunt the spindle-assembly checkpoint or the apoptotic response to mitotic arrest (e.g., ALK/EGFR-driven or mesenchymal-like lines). The strongest predictor is high KIF11/Eg5 expression and intact mitotic checkpoint signaling, with TP53 loss and proliferative driver mutations as sensitizing context.

features.basis: monastrol's annotated target; higher Eg5 levels increase dependence on its motor function
TP53-mutant lines dominate the most-killed set and are prone to mitotic catastrophe/apoptosis after spindle failure
KRAS-mutant pancreatic/gastric lines are enriched among sensitive lines, consistent with high proliferative drive
BRAF-mutant melanoma/thyroid/colorectal lines appear in the sensitive set
cell-cycle checkpoint loss accompanies several sensitive lines
ATM-mutant lines appear among sensitive cases, suggesting defective DNA-damage/mitotic checkpoint crosstalk
Aurora B activity is required to maintain the spindle checkpoint and can override monastrol-induced arrest
Plk1 supports spindle assembly and checkpoint silencing; high Plk1 may allow escape from monopolar arrest
Mad2 is activated at kinetochores in monastrol-treated cells and is required for the mitotic arrest
ALK-altered lung/mesothelioma/neuroblastoma lines are overrepresented among least-affected lines
EGFR-mutant NSCLC lines appear in the resistant set
SMARCA4-mutant COV434 is among the most killed lines, suggesting chromatin-remodeler loss increases mitotic vulnerability
